name: 90-90 Hip Rotation
steps: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent at 90 degrees, feet off the ground.
Extend your arms out to the sides for stability, palms facing down.
Keeping your knees together, slowly rotate your legs to one side until they are just above the floor.
Pause for a moment, then rotate your legs back through center and to the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The 90-90 rotation is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the abdominal muscles and obliques. It involves lying on your back with legs bent at 90 degrees and rotating them side to side, improving spinal rotation and core stability.

name: Air Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward.
Engage your core and push your hips back as you bend your knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest tall and your knees tracking over your toes.
Press through your heels to return to the standing position.
about: The air squat is a foundational bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It teaches proper squat mechanics and builds lower body strength, making it the basis for all squat progressions.

name: Archer Push-up
steps: Start in a wide push-up position with your hands significantly wider than shoulder-width.
Extend one arm straight out to the side, parallel to the ground.
Lower your body toward the bent arm, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Push back up to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, extending the opposite arm.
about: The archer push up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that targets the pectorals by placing more load on one arm at a time. The extended arm provides balance and mild assistance, making it a powerful stepping stone toward single-arm push-up strength.

name: Band Bent-over Row
steps: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and soft knees.
Pull the band toward your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly with control and repeat.

name: Band Deadlift
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the band at your sides with palms facing inward and hinge forward at the hips.
Keep your back flat and chest tall throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips to stand upright.
Pause at the top with hips fully extended.
about: The resistance band deadlift replicates the hip hinge pattern of a conventional deadlift using band resistance. It targets the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings while being accessible for home workouts or warm-up activation work.

name: Band Front Squat
steps: Stand on the band, holding the ends at your shoulders.
Sit hips back and down into a squat.
Keep chest up and knees tracking over toes.
Drive through heels to stand.

name: Band Glute Kickback
steps: Loop a resistance band around your ankles and get on all fours on a mat.
Keep your core engaged and spine neutral throughout the movement.
Kick one leg straight back, extending it fully until it is parallel to the ground.
Squeeze your glute at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired repetitions before switching legs.
about: The banded glute kick is a resistance band exercise performed on all fours, targeting the glutes and hamstrings. The band adds resistance to the kickback motion, intensifying glute activation and supporting hip extension development.

name: Band Good Morning
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band and place the looped ends over your shoulders.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge at your hips and lower your torso toward parallel while keeping your back flat.
Pause at the bottom, feeling the stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright position.
about: The resistance band good morning is a hip hinge exercise targeting the hamstrings using band resistance. It teaches proper posterior chain loading mechanics and is a gentler alternative to barbell good mornings for building hamstring and lower back strength.

name: Band High Side Pull
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp a resistance band with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and extend your arms straight up overhead.
Keep your core engaged and pull the band apart by driving your elbows down and out to the sides.
Bring the band down behind your neck until it reaches your upper back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly control the resistance as you raise your arms back to the starting overhead position.
about: The resistance band high side pull targets the deltoids and upper back through a diagonal pulling motion. The upward and lateral pulling path simultaneously engages the medial and posterior deltoids, improving shoulder strength and stability.

name: Band Lateral Raise
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold one end of the band in each hand with arms at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded lateral raise is a resistance band shoulder exercise targeting the lateral deltoids. The band provides progressive resistance as the arms rise, offering a unique stimulus compared to dumbbells and making it an effective portable shoulder exercise.

name: Band Lunge
steps: Stand with both feet on the center of a resistance band, holding the ends at shoulder height.
Step one foot forward into a lunge position, keeping your torso upright.
Lower your back knee toward the ground until both knees are at approximately 90 degrees.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the opposite leg and continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Band lunges are a resistance band exercise targeting the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. The band adds accommodating resistance throughout the lunge movement, increasing difficulty at the top and improving lower body strength and stability.

name: Band Monster Walk
steps: Place a resistance band around your ankles and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Slightly bend your knees and get into an athletic quarter-squat position.
Take a large step forward and to the right, maintaining tension in the band.
Follow with your left foot, keeping feet apart against the band resistance.
Continue walking forward for the desired distance, then reverse direction.
about: The resistance band monster walk is a glute activation exercise that targets the glute medius through lateral and forward stepping against band resistance. It improves hip abductor strength, knee stability, and is commonly used as a warm-up or corrective exercise.

name: Band One-Arm Row
steps: Anchor one end of a resistance band at a low point and stand to the side facing the anchor.
Hold the other end of the band in one hand with your arm extended toward the anchor.
Brace your core and hinge slightly at the hips with a flat back.
Pull the band toward your hip by driving your elbow back, squeezing your lat at the top.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired repetitions before switching arms.
about: The banded one arm row is a unilateral resistance band exercise targeting the lats and upper back. Performing one arm at a time allows for greater focus on muscle activation and helps address any strength imbalances between sides.

name: Band Overhead Pull-apart
steps: Stand tall holding a band with a wide grip, arms straight out at shoulder height.
Keeping arms straight, raise the band up overhead.
Lower it back to shoulder height while pulling the band apart and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Move slowly and keep your ribs down throughout.

name: Band Overhead Triceps Extension
steps: Assume a half-kneeling position with one knee on the floor, and anchor one end of the resistance band under that kneeling leg.
Grasp the other end of the band with both hands and extend your arms fully overhead.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your head, bend your elbows to slowly lower the hands behind your head.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Extend your arms back up to the starting position by straightening your elbows and squeezing your triceps.
about: The resistance band overhead triceps extension targets the long head of the triceps through an overhead extension movement. The band provides progressive resistance, making it an accessible and effective option for triceps development.

name: Band Pull-Apart
steps: Hold a band in front of your chest with straight arms, hands shoulder-width apart.
Squeeze your shoulder blades and pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Control the band back to the start without letting your shoulders shrug.

name: Band Shoulder Roll
steps: Hold a resistance band with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms at your sides.
Roll your shoulders forward in a circular motion while maintaining gentle tension on the band.
Complete several forward circles, then reverse the direction.
Keep the movements slow and controlled.
Repeat for the desired duration or repetitions.
about: The resistance band shoulder roll is a mobility and warm-up exercise targeting the deltoids and rotator cuff through circular shoulder rotation. The band adds light tension to increase activation and improve blood flow to the shoulder joint.

name: Band Squat with Lateral Raise
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends in each hand.
Lower into a squat as you hold the band handles at your sides.
As you press back up to standing, raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height against the band.
Lower your arms as you descend into the next squat.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The resistance band squat with lateral raise combines a lower body squat with an upper body lateral raise into a single movement. It simultaneously targets the quads and shoulders, making it a time-efficient full-body exercise.

name: Band Supine Hamstring Stretch
steps: Lie flat on your back on the floor.
Loop a resistance band or long strap around the arch of one foot, holding the ends of the band with your hands.
Keep your opposite leg resting flat on the floor.
Keeping the banded leg straight, use the band to help pull your leg upward toward the ceiling.
Raise the leg until you feel a stretch in your hamstring and hold briefly.
about: The resistance band supine hamstring stretch is a flexibility and mobility exercise targeting the hamstrings. By using a band, you can safely guide the leg into a deeper stretch while keeping the back flat and supported on the floor, improving posterior chain flexibility.

name: Band W-Raise
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ends of a resistance band with both hands.
Raise your arms in front of you at shoulder height with elbows slightly bent.
Pull the band apart and back, bending your elbows to form a W shape with your arms.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position.
about: The resistance band w-raise is an upper back and shoulder health exercise targeting the rhomboids and rear deltoids. The W arm position maximizes scapular retraction and external rotation, improving posture and rotator cuff stability.

name: Banded Biceps Curl
steps: Stand with both feet on the center of a resistance band, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold one end of the band in each hand with a supinated grip, arms hanging at your sides.
Keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso, curl your hands up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hands back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded biceps curl is a resistance band exercise targeting the biceps. Standing on the band and curling upward mimics the motion of a dumbbell curl while providing accommodating resistance throughout the range of motion.

name: Banded Donkey Kick
steps: Kneel on all fours with a band above your knees.
Keeping the knee bent, kick one leg back and up toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glute at the top, then lower with control.
Keep your back flat and complete reps before switching sides.

name: Banded Glute Bridge Abduction
steps: Loop a resistance band just above your knees and lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Drive through your heels to perform a glute bridge, thrusting your hips toward the ceiling.
At the top of the bridge, push your knees apart against the band in an abduction motion.
Bring your knees back together and lower your hips to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Thrust to abduction is a resistance band exercise that combines a glute bridge with a hip abduction movement. This compound glute exercise targets the gluteus maximus through the thrust and the gluteus medius through the outward knee press.

name: Banded Jumping Jack
steps: Place a resistance band around your ankles and stand with feet together.
Jump and spread your feet wide against the resistance of the band while raising your arms overhead.
Jump your feet back together.
Continue at a steady, controlled rhythm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The jumping jack with resistance band adds lateral resistance to a standard jumping jack, increasing adductor and abductor engagement. The band amplifies the cardio conditioning and lower body strengthening effects of the exercise.

name: Banded Lat Pulldown
steps: Anchor a resistance band overhead at a fixed point and kneel or sit below the anchor.
Grasp the band with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
With arms extended overhead, pull the band down toward your chest by driving your elbows toward your hips.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly allow your arms to extend back overhead and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded lat pulldown is a resistance band exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi. Anchoring the band overhead and pulling it downward mimics the cable lat pulldown, effectively engaging the lats, biceps, and rhomboids.

name: Banded Overhead Press
steps: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band at shoulder height with palms facing forward and elbows bent.
Press the band overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower your hands back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded overhead press is a shoulder exercise targeting the deltoids using resistance band tension for progressive resistance. It builds overhead pressing strength and shoulder stability while being gentle on the joints compared to barbell or dumbbell variations.

name: Banded Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a resistance band looped just above your knees.
Hold your hands in front of your chest for balance and push your knees out against the band.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, maintaining outward knee pressure against the band throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded squat is a resistance band exercise that targets the quads and glutes while activating the hip abductors. The band placed above the knees encourages proper knee tracking and adds an abductor challenge to the standard squat movement.

name: Bear Crawl
steps: On hands and feet with knees just off the floor.
Crawl forward. Log metres or seconds as reps.
about: The bear crawl is a full-body cardio and strength exercise performed in a low quadruped position. It elevates heart rate while engaging the shoulders, core, and legs simultaneously, making it an effective conditioning and functional movement exercise.

name: Bear Hold
steps: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees directly under your hips.
Tuck your toes under and lift your knees just a few centimeters off the ground.
Keep your back flat, core braced, and hold this position.
Maintain steady breathing and avoid letting your hips rise or sag.
Hold for the desired duration.
about: The bear hold is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs and core stabilizers. By hovering the knees just above the ground in an all-fours position, this movement builds deep core strength, shoulder stability, and body awareness.

name: Bicycle Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with your hands placed behind your head and your knees bent.
Lift your shoulders off the ground and raise your legs to a 90-degree angle.
Bring your right elbow toward your left knee while simultaneously extending your right leg.
Switch sides in a controlled pedaling motion, bringing your left elbow toward your right knee.
Continue alternating in a smooth, rhythmic motion for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The bicycle is a bodyweight core exercise that targets the abs and obliques simultaneously. The alternating elbow-to-knee pedaling motion creates rotational tension across the entire core, making it one of the most effective abdominal exercises.

name: Bird Dog
steps: On all fours, extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Hold briefly, then switch sides.
about: The bird dog is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and lower back, with secondary engagement of the abs and glutes. It involves alternately extending opposite arm and leg from a quadruped position to develop core stability, balance, and spinal control.

name: Bird Dog Double Arm Reach
steps: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Engage your core to stabilize your spine and keep your back flat.
Simultaneously raise both arms straight forward while extending both legs behind you, balancing on your torso.
Hold the position for 2-3 seconds, maintaining a neutral spine and avoiding rotation.
Lower back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The bird dog advanced (both hands raise) is a challenging bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and lower back, with secondary engagement of the abs and glutes. It involves simultaneously lifting both arms and both legs from a tabletop position, demanding exceptional core stability and balance.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench or elevated surface and place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Ensure your front foot is far enough forward that your knee does not travel past your toes during the descent.
Engage your core and lower your back knee towards the ground by bending your front leg.
Descend until your front thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
about: The Bulgarian split squat is a bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary emphasis on the glutes and hamstrings. It is performed with the rear foot elevated, creating a unilateral loading pattern that challenges leg strength, stability, and hip mobility.

name: Burpee
steps: Drop into a push-up, touch your chest to the floor.
Jump your feet in and leap up with arms overhead.
about: The burpee is a full-body bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and cardiovascular system, with secondary engagement of the chest, quads, and shoulders. It combines a squat, plank, push-up, and jump into one continuous movement, making it highly effective for conditioning and calorie expenditure.

name: Burpee to Broad Jump
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop your hands to the ground and jump or step your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then jump your feet back toward your hands.
From a crouched position, swing your arms back and then explosively jump forward as far as possible.
Land softly with bent knees and immediately reset for the next repetition.
about: The burpee to broad jump is a full-body plyometric exercise that combines the conditioning demands of a burpee with an explosive horizontal jump. It targets the quadriceps and glutes while also developing total-body power, cardiovascular endurance, and coordination.

name: Burpee to Tuck Jump
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop your hands to the ground and jump or step your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then explosively jump your feet back toward your hands.
From a crouched position, leap vertically and drive your knees toward your chest in a tuck position.
Land softly with bent knees and immediately begin the next repetition.
about: The burpee to tuck jump is an advanced plyometric exercise combining the full-body conditioning of a burpee with an explosive vertical tuck jump. It targets the quadriceps and glutes while developing power, coordination, and cardiovascular fitness.

name: Butt Kick
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and begin jogging in place.
Increase the range of motion by kicking your heels up toward your glutes with each step.
Pump your arms in coordination with your legs.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: Butt kicks are a cardio and hamstring activation exercise performed by jogging in place with an exaggerated heel-to-glute kick. They are commonly used as a dynamic warm-up or cardio drill to engage the hamstrings and elevate the heart rate.

name: Butt Kick (Low Impact)
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Lift one heel toward your glutes by bending your knee, keeping your thighs parallel.
Lower that foot and repeat with the opposite leg in an alternating marching pattern.
Keep the movement controlled and low impact, avoiding jumping.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: Butt kick low impact is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the hamstrings through a controlled heel-to-glute movement. The low-impact marching variation reduces joint stress while warming up the hamstrings and gently elevating the heart rate.

name: Cat-Cow Stretch
steps: Start on all fours with your wrists directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Inhale and drop your belly toward the floor while lifting your chest and tailbone upward (cow position).
Exhale and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat position).
Continue alternating between cat and cow positions in a slow, controlled rhythm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The cat cow back stretch is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the lower back and spine through alternating extension and flexion. It improves spinal flexibility, reduces tension, and is commonly used in warm-up and rehabilitation routines.

name: Child's Pose
steps: Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees hip-width apart.
Sit back onto your heels, then fold your torso forward and extend your arms straight out in front of you on the floor.
Rest your forehead gently on the ground and relax your shoulders toward the floor.
Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply and allowing your back to lengthen.
Slowly walk your hands back in and rise to the starting position.
about: Child pose is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the lats, with secondary engagement of the lower back and glutes. It involves folding the torso forward from a kneeling position to gently decompress the spine and release tension throughout the back.

name: Clap Push-up
steps: Begin in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled manner, keeping your body in a straight line.
Explosively push up with maximum force so your hands leave the ground.
While airborne, quickly clap your hands together, then return your hands to the floor to catch yourself.
Absorb the landing with slightly bent elbows and immediately begin the next repetition.
about: The clap push up is an advanced bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the chest, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, upper arms, and abs. It involves an explosive push-up that generates enough force to clap the hands mid-air, developing upper body power and fast-twitch muscle activation.

name: Close Grip Push-up
steps: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed directly under your chest, closer than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides throughout the movement.
Lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled manner, keeping your core engaged and your body in a straight line.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press through your palms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Close grip push ups are a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest with increased emphasis on the upper arms. The narrow hand position shifts the workload to the triceps and inner chest, making this a highly effective compound pressing movement.

name: Cossack Squat
steps: Stand with your feet in a wide stance and toes pointed slightly outward.
Shift your weight to your right side and bend your right knee, lowering your hips toward the floor.
Extend your left leg out to the side, keeping it straight with your foot flat on the floor.
Pause at the bottom of the movement, feeling the stretch in your inner thigh.
Drive through your right heel to return to the starting position.
about: The cossack squat is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hip adductors and inner thighs. The deep lateral squat with an extended opposite leg develops hip mobility, inner thigh flexibility, and single-leg strength.

name: Crab Walk
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat, and hands planted behind your hips with fingers pointing forward.
Lift your hips off the floor to enter the crab position.
Move forward or backward by coordinating opposite hand and foot movements.
Keep your hips elevated and core engaged throughout.
Continue for the desired distance or duration.
about: The crab walk is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes through a reverse table-top locomotion pattern. It builds hip extension strength, shoulder stability, and full-body coordination while keeping the hips elevated off the floor.

name: Cross Country Jacks
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders.
Drive your right knee toward your left elbow in a cross-body motion.
Return to the starting position and repeat with your left knee toward your right elbow.
Alternate sides in a continuous, controlled running motion.
Maintain a flat back and engaged core throughout.
about: Cross country is a dynamic core and cardio exercise performed in a plank position that mimics a cross-body running motion. It targets the cardiovascular system while engaging the core, hip flexors, and lower body for a challenging conditioning workout.

name: Cross-Body Knee Crunch
steps: Begin in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body straight.
Bring your right knee across your body toward your left elbow.
Return your foot to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, bringing your left knee toward your right elbow.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The cross-body knee crunch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the obliques through a diagonal knee drive from a plank position. The cross-body movement pattern challenges rotational core stability and hip flexor strength simultaneously.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
steps: Stand or sit upright with your back straight and core engaged.
Extend one arm straight across your body at chest height.
Use your opposite forearm or hand to press the arm gently toward your chest.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling tension in the back of your shoulder.
Release and repeat on the other side.
about: The cross-body shoulder stretch is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the posterior deltoids, with secondary engagement of the traps and upper arms. It involves pulling one arm horizontally across the body to release tightness in the shoulder and improve joint flexibility.

name: Cross-body Arm Swing
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Swing one arm across your chest while the other swings out to the side.
Switch sides in a smooth, controlled rhythm.
Keep shoulders relaxed and breathe steadily.

name: Cross-body Mountain Climber
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and drive your right knee toward your left elbow.
Return your right foot to the starting position, then immediately drive your left knee toward your right elbow.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled, rhythmic motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: Cross-body mountain climbers are a dynamic bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and obliques. By driving each knee to the opposite elbow, the movement adds a rotational element that intensifies core engagement and raises the heart rate.

name: Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed lightly behind your head.
Engage your core and curl your upper body off the floor toward your knees.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The standard crunch is a foundational bodyweight abdominal exercise that targets the abs through spinal flexion. It is widely used as a core strength builder and can be performed by individuals of all fitness levels.

name: Crunch Hug
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Wrap your arms around your knees, hugging them toward your chest.
Curl your upper body off the ground toward your knees, engaging your abs.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your core.
Slowly lower back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The crunch hug is a bodyweight abdominal exercise that combines a traditional crunch with a knee tuck. Wrapping the arms around the knees while crunching upward intensifies abdominal engagement and promotes core compression.

name: Curtsy Lunge
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step one leg diagonally behind the other and bend both knees into a lunge.
Keep your chest up and front knee over the ankle.
Push through the front heel to return and switch sides.

name: Dead Bug
steps: Lie on your back with arms and knees up.
Extend the opposite arm and leg, then switch.
about: The dead bug is a bodyweight core stability exercise that targets the abs while teaching proper spinal bracing. By moving opposite limbs simultaneously, it challenges coordination and deep core control while minimizing lower back stress.

name: Dead Bug (Legs Only)
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms flat by your sides and knees bent at 90 degrees, feet off the floor.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your core.
Slowly extend one leg toward the floor, keeping it just above the surface.
Return that leg to the bent position and extend the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The dead bug legs only is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles by isolating the leg extension component of the classic dead bug. Removing the arm movement allows full focus on lower abdominal engagement and spinal stability.

name: Decline Push-up
steps: Place your feet on an elevated surface such as a bench or step and position your hands on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from head to heels with your core engaged.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom when your chest is just above the floor.
Press back up to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Decline push ups are a bodyweight exercise targeting the upper chest, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, upper arms, and abs. By elevating the feet, the angle shifts the emphasis onto the upper portion of the pectoral muscles and increases overall difficulty.

name: Diamond Cobra Push-up
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands forming a diamond shape under your chest.
Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
At the bottom, lower your hips to the ground and extend your arms, arching your back into a cobra stretch.
Return your hips upward and bend your elbows to lower back into the bottom of the push-up.
Push back up to the starting position.
about: The diamond cobra push up combines a close-grip diamond push-up with a cobra extension at the bottom of each rep. It targets the pectorals and triceps during the pressing phase while stretching the lower back and core through the cobra movement.

name: Diamond Push-up
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed close together beneath your chest, forming a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers.
Keep your body in a straight line and engage your core.
Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows.
Pause just above the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
about: The close grip diamond push-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps with secondary pectoral involvement. The narrow hand placement intensifies triceps engagement and inner chest activation compared to a standard push-up.

name: Dolphin Plank
steps: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly beneath your shoulders and forearms flat on the floor.
Engage your core, glutes, and legs to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Press your forearms firmly into the floor and keep your hips level, avoiding any sagging or piking.
Hold the position for the desired duration while breathing steadily.
Release by lowering your knees to the floor.
about: The dolphin plank hold is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders and lower back. It is performed in a forearm plank position, requiring sustained core and shoulder stability to maintain proper alignment throughout the hold.

name: Donkey Kick
steps: Start on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Keep your right knee bent at 90 degrees and flex your right foot.
Push your right heel upward toward the ceiling while squeezing your glute.
Pause at the top of the movement, fully contracting your glute.
Lower your knee back toward the floor without touching it.
about: The donkey single leg kick is a bodyweight glute exercise performed on all fours. By kicking one heel upward with the knee bent, it isolates the gluteus maximus and is commonly used as a glute activation exercise in warm-up and lower body routines.

name: Downward Dog
steps: Begin in a plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and fingers spread wide.
Press through your palms and lift your hips toward the ceiling, straightening your legs and lowering your heels toward the floor.
Your body should form an inverted V-shape with your head positioned between your arms.
Engage your core and press your chest gently toward your thighs to deepen the shoulder stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily, then return to the starting position.
about: The downward dog hold is a bodyweight stretching and strengthening exercise targeting the deltoids, with secondary engagement of the lats, hamstrings, and lower back. It involves holding an inverted V-shape position to simultaneously stretch the posterior chain and build shoulder and core stability.

name: Dynamic Arm Swings
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms resting by your sides.
Engage your core and keep your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly raise both arms out to your sides simultaneously.
Continue lifting until your arms are fully extended and parallel to the floor, keeping your palms facing down.
Pause and hold this extended position briefly.
about: Dynamic arms stretch is a bodyweight warm-up and mobility exercise targeting the deltoids, with secondary engagement of the traps, chest, and upper arms. It involves performing controlled arm circles in both directions to increase shoulder joint mobility and blood flow to the upper body.

name: Dynamic Side Stretch
steps: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
Raise both arms overhead, keeping your elbows slightly bent so your hands frame your head.
Engage your core and slowly bend your torso to one side, keeping your chest facing forward.
Pause briefly when you feel a stretch along the side of your body.
Slowly return to the upright center position.
about: The dynamic upper body stretch is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the chest, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, traps, and lats. It involves sweeping the arms in a wide arc to open the chest and loosen the upper body, making it an effective warm-up or cool-down movement.

name: Elbow Wall Plank
steps: Stand facing a wall and place your forearms against it at shoulder height, elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Step your feet back until your body forms a straight diagonal line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, keeping your hips level.
Avoid letting your lower back sag or your hips rise.
Hold for the desired duration.
about: The elbow wall plank is a bodyweight isometric exercise that targets the abdominal muscles in a modified upright position. It is commonly used as a beginner-friendly alternative to the floor plank, building core endurance and stability.

name: Fast Feet
steps: Stand in a low athletic stance with your knees slightly bent, feet hip-width apart, and your weight on the balls of your feet.
Lower your hips slightly as if in a quarter squat, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Begin rapidly alternating your feet in short, quick steps while maintaining the low stance.
Pump your arms quickly to drive the pace of your feet.
Continue for the desired duration, keeping the tempo as fast as possible throughout.
about: Fast feet sprint in low stance is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the hamstrings, glutes, and lower legs. It involves rapid foot shuffles from a low athletic position to develop speed, agility, and cardiovascular endurance.

name: Fingertip Push-up
steps: Begin in a standard push-up position but support your weight on your fingertips instead of your palms.
Spread your fingers wide for maximum stability.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Pause at the bottom, then press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The fingers push-up is an advanced bodyweight variation of the standard push-up that shifts weight onto the fingertips. This modification dramatically increases forearm and grip strength demands while maintaining the chest and triceps activation of a standard push-up.

name: Fire Hydrant
steps: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Keep your right knee bent at 90 degrees and lift it out to the side.
Raise your knee as high as your hip level while keeping your back flat.
Pause at the top, squeezing your outer glute.
Slowly lower your knee back to the starting position.
about: The fire hydrant is a bodyweight glute exercise performed on all fours that targets the glute medius and outer glutes through a lateral hip abduction movement. It is widely used for glute activation, hip mobility, and rehabilitation purposes.

name: Flutter Kick
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and hands placed beneath your lower back for support.
Lift both legs a few inches off the ground, engaging your core.
Alternately raise and lower each leg in a small, controlled fluttering motion.
Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor throughout the movement.
Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: The flutter kick is a bodyweight core exercise targeting the abs and hip flexors through continuous alternating leg movements. Performed lying on the back, it builds lower abdominal endurance and overall core stability.

name: Forearm Plank
steps: Place your forearms on the ground with elbows directly below your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet.
Align your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core.
Keep your hips level and avoid sagging or raising your lower back.
Hold this position for the desired duration.
about: The standard plank is a fundamental isometric bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and core. Held on the forearms, it simultaneously engages the shoulders, lower back, and glutes, making it one of the most effective exercises for full core stability.

name: Forward Lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and your hands on your hips or hanging by your sides.
Step one foot forward into a wide stance and lower your back knee toward the floor by bending both legs.
Descend until your front thigh is approximately parallel to the floor and your back knee hovers just above the ground.
Drive through your front heel to push back to the starting position.
Alternate legs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Forward lunges are a bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes and hamstrings. The movement involves stepping forward and lowering the hips in an alternating pattern, developing unilateral leg strength, balance, and coordination.

name: Frog Pump
steps: Lie on your back with soles of feet together.
Thrust your hips up quickly, squeeze, lower.
about: Frog pumps are a bodyweight glute isolation exercise performed with feet together and knees flared outward. The external rotation of the hips shifts the focus to the gluteal muscles, making it an effective activation and warm-up movement.

name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze at the top, then lower.
about: The glute bridge is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary engagement of the hamstrings, lower back, and abs. It involves lifting the hips from a supine position to strengthen the posterior chain, improve hip extension, and stabilize the core.

name: Glute Bridge Hold
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms flat on the floor beside you, palms facing down.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes firmly at the top.
Hold this position for the desired duration, maintaining steady breathing.
about: The glute bridge hold is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the glutes. Holding the bridge position develops glute endurance and strength while also engaging the hamstrings and core stabilizers.

name: Glute Bridge March
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the ground, hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a glute bridge position.
Maintaining the bridge height with your hips, lift one knee toward your chest in a marching motion.
Lower the foot back to the ground and repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The glute bridge march is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes while challenging core stability and hip flexor control. Holding a sustained bridge while alternating knee lifts requires the glutes and core to work together dynamically.

name: Glute Bridge Walkout
steps: Loop a resistance band just above your knees and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a quarter squat position and push your knees outward against the band.
Take a step to one side with your right foot, then bring your left foot to follow.
Continue stepping laterally for the desired number of steps, then reverse direction.
Keep tension on the band throughout and maintain the squat position during all steps.
about: The glute walk is a resistance band exercise that targets the gluteus medius and hip abductors through lateral banded walking. Maintaining a squat position while resisting the band encourages continuous glute activation and improves hip stability.

name: Half Reverse Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with your hands placed beneath your lower back and legs bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and slowly draw your knees toward your chest, lifting your hips slightly off the floor.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your legs back to the 90-degree starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The half reverse crunch is a bodyweight ab exercise that focuses on the lower abdominal region by curling the hips toward the chest. It provides a controlled range of motion suitable for building foundational core strength.

name: Half Sit-up
steps: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed behind your head.
Engage your core and curl your upper body upward until your torso reaches a 45-degree angle.
Pause briefly at the halfway point, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor.
Slowly lower your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Half sit ups are a beginner-friendly bodyweight ab exercise that targets the abs through a partial range of motion. By stopping midway, the movement maintains continuous tension on the abdominal muscles while reducing strain on the lower back.

name: Heel Slides
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and a smooth surface or sliders under your heels.
Brace your core and slowly slide both heels toward your glutes by bending your knees.
Once your heels are close to your glutes, slowly slide them back out to the starting position.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Heel slides are a bodyweight rehabilitation and activation exercise targeting the hamstrings. The controlled sliding motion through the full range of knee flexion and extension is commonly used to restore leg strength after injury.

name: Heel Tap
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lift your shoulders slightly off the ground, engaging your abs.
Reach your right hand down to tap your right heel, crunching to the side.
Return to center and repeat on the left side, reaching your left hand to your left heel.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The heel tap is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques. By lying on your back and alternately reaching to tap each heel, it creates a lateral crunch motion that strengthens the sides of the core.

name: High Knee Butt Kick
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and begin jogging in place.
Alternate between driving your knees up toward your chest and kicking your heels up toward your glutes with each stride.
Pump your arms in coordination with your legs to maintain an athletic rhythm.
Keep your core engaged and your posture upright throughout the movement.
Continue alternating for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: High knee butt kick is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the quadriceps and hamstrings, with secondary engagement of the glutes and lower legs. It combines high knee drives with heel kicks in an alternating running pattern to elevate heart rate and warm up the lower body dynamically.

name: High Knees
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and begin jogging in place.
Drive your right knee upward toward your chest as high as possible.
Quickly switch legs, driving your left knee upward.
Pump your arms in coordination with each knee drive.
Continue alternating at a brisk pace for the desired duration.
about: High knees are a dynamic cardio exercise that combines running in place with exaggerated knee lifts. They engage the hip flexors and core while building cardiovascular endurance and lower body coordination.

name: High Plank
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands directly below your shoulders and arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads to maintain a rigid position.
Avoid sagging your hips or raising your lower back.
Hold for the desired duration.
about: The high plank is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs and core while performed on extended arms. Compared to the forearm plank, it places additional demand on the shoulders and triceps, making it a versatile full-body stability movement.

name: Hollow Hold
steps: Lie on your back, press your lower back down and lift arms and legs.
Hold. Log seconds as reps.
about: The hollow hold is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the lower back and hip flexors. It involves maintaining a curved body position with arms and legs raised off the floor, demanding sustained core compression and stability.

name: Inchworm
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Walk your hands forward one at a time until you reach a full plank position.
Hold the plank briefly, then walk your hands back toward your feet.
Stand back up and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The inchworm walkout is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, hamstrings, and lower back. It involves walking the hands out from a standing forward fold into a plank and back, warming up the entire body and challenging core and shoulder stability.

name: Jog in Place
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Begin jogging in place by alternating lifting each foot off the ground.
Maintain a light, bouncy rhythm on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms naturally to match your leg movement.
Continue for the desired duration.
about: Place jogging is a simple cardio exercise performed in a stationary position. It elevates the heart rate and warms up the lower body by simulating the movement pattern of running without requiring space or equipment.

name: Jump Lunge
steps: Start in a lunge position with your right foot forward and left foot back, both knees bent at 90 degrees.
Explosively jump upward, switching the positions of your feet mid-air.
Land softly with your left foot forward and right foot back in a lunge position.
Immediately lower into the lunge and jump again.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Jump lunges are a bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the quadriceps and developing explosive lower body power. The airborne switch between lunge positions increases cardiovascular demand and challenges balance and coordination.

name: Jump Squat
steps: Squat down quickly.
Explode up into a jump and land softly.
about: The jump squat is a plyometric exercise that combines a bodyweight squat with an explosive jump. It develops lower body power, fast-twitch muscle fiber activation, and cardiovascular conditioning.

name: Jumping Jack
steps: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet outward to slightly wider than shoulder-width apart while simultaneously raising your arms out to the sides and overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then jump your feet back together while lowering your arms to your sides.
Maintain a rhythmic, continuous pace throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The jumping jack is a classic bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, lower legs, and glutes. It involves simultaneous lateral jumping and arm raising in a rhythmic pattern to elevate heart rate and develop cardiovascular endurance.

name: Jumping Jack with High Knee
steps: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump your feet outward while raising your arms overhead as in a standard jumping jack.
Jump your feet back together, then immediately drive one knee up toward your chest.
Lower that foot and perform another jumping jack, then drive the opposite knee up on the return.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The jumping jack with high knee is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the abs, hip flexors, and lower legs. It combines the lateral jumping motion of a jumping jack with an alternating high knee drive to increase intensity and challenge coordination.

name: Kickboxing
steps: Stand in a fighting stance with one foot slightly forward and hands raised to guard position.
Throw a series of punches including jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts.
Alternate with front kicks, side kicks, and roundhouse kicks.
Maintain footwork and movement throughout the combination.
Continue for rounds of the desired duration.
about: Kickboxing is a high-intensity cardio workout that combines boxing punches and martial arts kicks. It develops cardiovascular fitness, coordination, agility, and total body conditioning through fast-paced offensive and defensive combinations.

name: Knee Lift Crunch
steps: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your hands behind your head.
Lift your right knee toward your chest while simultaneously crunching your left elbow toward the rising knee.
Lower your leg and return to the upright position.
Repeat on the opposite side, lifting your left knee and crunching your right elbow toward it.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The knee lift crunch is a standing bodyweight exercise that targets the abs and obliques. Alternating knee lifts combined with rotational crunches create a dynamic core movement that also engages the hip flexors.

name: Knee Push-up
steps: Kneel on the floor and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower your hips so your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Knee push-ups are a beginner bodyweight exercise targeting the pectoral muscles. By supporting the body on the knees rather than the toes, the movement reduces difficulty and allows those building upper body strength to practice proper push-up mechanics.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee with your other foot planted flat on the floor in front of you, creating a 90-degree angle at both knees.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core.
Gently shift your weight forward, pushing your front hip toward the floor until you feel a stretch in the front of your rear hip.
Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
Release and repeat on the other side.
about: The hip flexor stretch kneeling is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the quadriceps and hip flexors, with secondary engagement of the hamstrings and glutes. Performed in a kneeling lunge position, it effectively lengthens the hip flexor muscles, which are commonly tight from prolonged sitting.

name: Knuckle Push-up
steps: Begin in a push-up position but make fists with both hands and place your knuckles on the floor, aligned under your shoulders.
Keep your wrists neutral and straight throughout the movement.
Lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled manner, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Knuckle push ups are a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest, with secondary engagement of the upper arms, shoulders, and lower arms. Performing push ups on the knuckles maintains neutral wrist alignment, reduces wrist strain, and increases the range of motion during the descent.

name: L-Sit Hold
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Place your hands flat on the floor beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Press through your palms to lift your entire body off the floor, keeping your legs straight and parallel to the ground.
Hold the L-shape position for as long as possible, engaging your abs and keeping your back straight.
Slowly lower back down to the floor and rest before repeating.
about: The L-sit hold is an advanced bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors, upper arms, and shoulders. It involves suspending the body off the floor in an L-shape by pressing through the hands, requiring tremendous core compression and upper body pressing strength.

name: Lateral Bear Crawl
steps: Start in a bear hold position on all fours with knees hovering just above the ground.
Brace your core and move laterally by stepping your right hand and right foot out simultaneously.
Follow with your left hand and left foot to maintain your width.
Continue crawling sideways for the desired distance, then switch directions.
Keep your hips low and back flat throughout the movement.
about: The lateral bear crawl is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and shoulder stabilizers through sideways movement in a hovering all-fours position. It develops coordination, core stability, and shoulder endurance.

name: Lateral Lunge
steps: Stand with feet together and hands on your hips.
Take a wide step out to your right side and bend your right knee as you lower your body.
Keep your left leg straight and your right knee tracking over your right foot.
Lower until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting position.
about: The lateral lunge is a bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quads through a sideways stepping and squatting motion. It also stretches the adductors and strengthens the glutes, making it effective for developing frontal plane movement and hip mobility.

name: Lateral Shuffle
steps: Stand in a low athletic stance with your knees slightly bent and your weight on the balls of your feet.
Push off your inside foot and shuffle laterally in one direction by stepping and bringing your feet together repeatedly.
Keep your hips low and your chest up throughout the movement.
After the desired distance, plant your outside foot and shuffle back in the opposite direction.
Continue shuffling back and forth for the desired duration.
about: Lateral sprint shuffles are a bodyweight cardio and agility exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes, hamstrings, and lower legs. They involve rapid side-to-side shuffling in a low athletic stance to develop lateral speed, footwork, and cardiovascular conditioning.

name: Lateral Walking Lunge
steps: Stand with feet together and hands on your hips or extended in front.
Step one foot out wide to the side and lower into a lateral lunge by shifting your weight over that foot.
Keep the opposite leg straight and both feet flat on the ground.
Push off the bent leg to bring your feet back together.
Repeat in the same direction for the desired steps, then switch sides.
about: Lateral walking lunges are a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps and glutes through a side-to-side lunge pattern. They improve frontal plane strength, hip abductor activation, and dynamic balance.

name: Leg Swing Front to Back
steps: Stand on one leg with your hand on a wall or support for balance.
Engage your core and swing the free leg forward to hip height, then smoothly swing it behind you as far as comfortably possible.
Keep the movement controlled and use momentum to gradually increase your range of motion.
Complete the desired number of swings, then switch legs and repeat.
about: Leg swing front to back is a bodyweight dynamic stretching exercise targeting the hamstrings, with secondary engagement of the glutes and hip flexors. It involves rhythmically swinging one leg forward and backward to warm up the hip joint and improve sagittal plane mobility.

name: Leg Swing Side to Side
steps: Stand sideways next to a wall or support and place one hand on it for balance.
Engage your core and swing the free leg across your body to the opposite side, then swing it outward as far as comfortably possible.
Keep the swinging motion controlled and allow momentum to gradually open the range of motion.
Complete the desired number of swings, then turn around and repeat on the other leg.
about: Leg swing side to side is a bodyweight dynamic stretching exercise targeting the glutes and hip abductors, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors and lower back. It involves swinging one leg laterally across and away from the body to improve frontal plane hip mobility.

name: Lunge Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Stand with your feet together and your hands on your hips.
Step one foot forward and lower into a lunge until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
At the bottom of the lunge, tilt your pelvis slightly posteriorly to feel an increased stretch in the front of your rear hip.
Hold for 2-3 seconds at the bottom, then drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Hips flexor lunges are a bodyweight exercise targeting the quadriceps and hip flexors, with secondary engagement of the glutes and hamstrings. They combine a forward lunge with a posterior pelvic tilt at the bottom to actively stretch and strengthen the hip flexors through a full range of motion.

name: Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands beneath your lower back or flat on the floor.
Keep your legs together and raise them upward until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Pause at the top, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your legs back toward the floor without fully touching it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The lying leg lift up is a bodyweight ab and hip flexor exercise targeting the lower abdominals through a vertical leg raise. It builds lower core strength and hip flexor endurance while requiring the upper abs to stabilize the spine.

name: Lying Leg Raise (Bent Knee)
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your hands placed beneath your lower back or flat at your sides.
Bend your knees to approximately 90 degrees and lift your feet slightly off the ground.
Raise your bent legs upward, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Pause at the top, engaging your abs.
Slowly lower your feet back toward the ground without fully resting them and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The lying leg raise with bent knees is a bodyweight core exercise targeting the lower abs and hip flexors. Bending the knees reduces the lever arm compared to a straight-leg raise, making it more accessible while still effectively loading the abdominal muscles.

name: Mountain Climber
steps: Start in a push-up position.
Drive your knees toward your chest one at a time, quickly.
about: The mountain climber is a bodyweight cardio and core exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, quads, and hip flexors. It involves rapidly alternating knee drives in a plank position to challenge core stability, cardiovascular endurance, and overall conditioning.

name: Neck Half Circles
steps: Sit or stand with your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly drop your chin toward your chest.
Gently roll your head in a half arc from one shoulder toward the other, passing through the center.
Pause briefly on each side when your ear approaches your shoulder, feeling the stretch in your neck.
Return to center and repeat in the other direction for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Neck half circle is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the neck muscles, with secondary engagement of the traps. It involves rolling the head in a controlled half-circle motion to release tension along the cervical spine and improve neck mobility.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneel on a mat with your ankles anchored under a sofa or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from knees to head.
Lower forward as slowly as you can, resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands, then push back to the start.

name: One-Arm Push-up
steps: Start in a push-up position and widen your feet for extra stability.
Place one hand on the floor beneath your shoulder and place the other hand behind your back.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your working elbow.
Keep your body as square as possible throughout the movement.
Press back up to the starting position.
about: The one hand push-up is an elite bodyweight exercise targeting the pectorals and triceps with maximum load on a single arm. It requires exceptional upper body strength, core stability, and balance to perform with proper form.

name: Over Under Shoulder Reach
steps: Kneel on the floor with your torso upright and your core engaged.
Place one hand behind your head and the opposite hand behind your lower back.
Simultaneously extend both arms outward to your sides, straightening your elbows.
Sweep your arms to reverse the position, placing the opposite hand behind your head and the other behind your lower back.
Continue alternating this over-and-under motion smoothly for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The over under is a bodyweight agility and core exercise targeting the obliques through lateral bending and rotation. Ducking alternately to each side challenges lateral core strength, balance, and coordination.

name: Overhead Arm Sweep
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms resting naturally at your sides.
Engage your core and maintain a straight posture.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, slowly sweep both arms out to the sides and upward in a wide arc.
Continue raising your arms until they are extended overhead.
Smoothly reverse the motion, sweeping your arms back down to your sides.
about: The dynamic overhead arm sweep is a bodyweight mobility exercise that targets the deltoids, chest, and upper back. By moving the arms through a wide, lateral arc to an overhead position, it actively improves shoulder joint flexibility and blood flow, making it an excellent warm-up movement.

name: Pelvic Tilt
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Flatten your lower back against the floor by tightening your abdominal muscles and tilting your pelvis slightly upward.
Hold this position for a few seconds, keeping your glutes relaxed.
Release and allow your lower back to return to its natural arch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The pelvic tilt is a bodyweight rehabilitation exercise targeting the abdominal muscles and lower back. This gentle movement is commonly used to reduce lower back pain, improve lumbopelvic stability, and develop core awareness.

name: Pike Push-up
steps: Get into a pike with hips high and hands on the floor.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Push back up.
about: The pike push-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the deltoids in a vertical pressing pattern. The elevated hip position shifts the load away from the chest and onto the shoulders, making it an effective progression toward handstand push-ups.

name: Pistol Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other out in front.
Squat down on the standing leg, then stand back up.
about: The pistol squat is an advanced bodyweight exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes, hamstrings, and abs. It is a single-leg squat performed to full depth while the opposite leg is held straight out, demanding exceptional unilateral strength, balance, and ankle flexibility.

name: Plank Hip Dip
steps: Start in a forearm plank position with your elbows beneath your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and slowly rotate your hips to the right, dipping toward the floor.
Return to the center plank position before dipping your hips to the left.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The plank hip dip is a bodyweight core exercise that targets the abs and obliques through controlled lateral hip rotation. Performed from the forearm plank position, it adds rotational challenge to standard plank stability, increasing oblique activation.

name: Plank In and Out Jump
steps: Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet outward to shoulder-width apart while simultaneously bringing your arms up.
Immediately jump your feet back together.
Continue alternating in and out at a rapid pace.
Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: The in and out jump is a plyometric bodyweight exercise that targets the quads, glutes, and hip abductors. The rapid inward and outward jumping motion elevates the heart rate and builds lower body power and agility.

name: Plank Jack
steps: Begin in a forearm or high plank position with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your hips stable throughout.
Jump both feet out to the sides simultaneously, landing wider than hip-width apart.
Immediately jump both feet back together to the starting position.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions at a controlled pace.
about: The plank jack is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, glutes, and lower legs. It combines the stability demands of a plank with a lateral jumping motion of the feet to add a cardiovascular component while training core endurance.

name: Plank Jack Step-Out
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and jump both feet out wider than hip-width.
Immediately jump your feet back together.
Continue the in-and-out jumping motion at a controlled pace.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The plank jack modification is a cardio and core exercise that combines the stability demands of a plank with the heart rate elevation of a jumping jack. By keeping the upper body fixed, it targets the shoulders and abs while conditioning the lower body.

name: Plank Rotation Reach
steps: Start in a high plank.
Rotate your chest open and sweep one arm up toward the ceiling.
Return the hand to the floor under your shoulder.
Repeat on the other side.

name: Plank Tuck Jump
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Jump both feet forward, driving knees toward chest.
Jump feet back to plank.
Keep your core tight and hips level.

name: Plank to Downward Dog
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Push your hips up and back into a downward dog position, forming an inverted V shape.
Press your heels toward the floor and lengthen through your spine.
Pause at the top, feeling the stretch through your back and hamstrings.
Return to the plank position.
about: Plank to downward dog is a bodyweight mobility and strength exercise that transitions between a plank and an inverted V position. It stretches the lower back and hamstrings while strengthening the shoulders and core through the transition.

name: Plank with Reach
steps: Begin in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body forming a straight line.
Brace your core and slowly lift one arm off the ground, extending it directly in front of you.
Hold briefly while maintaining a stable plank position with minimal hip rotation.
Return your hand to the floor and repeat on the other arm.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The plank with reach is a bodyweight exercise that adds dynamic challenge to the standard plank by requiring alternating arm extensions. This movement demands strong anti-rotation core stability and shoulder control.

name: Prone Arm Sweep
steps: Lie face down with arms stretched overhead and legs long.
Lift your chest, arms and legs slightly off the floor.
Sweep your arms out wide and back by your sides, then return overhead.
Keep your neck long and glutes squeezed throughout.
about: The prone back extension is a foundational bodyweight exercise targeting the lower back erectors through a spinal extension movement. Performed lying face down, it is commonly used in rehabilitation and warm-up routines to strengthen the posterior chain.

name: Push-up
steps: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and fingers pointing forward.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the floor, then press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The standard push up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise targeting the chest, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, upper arms, and abs. It involves lowering and pressing the body in a plank position to develop upper body pushing strength and core stability.

name: Push-up Arm Lift
steps: Start in a standard push-up position with hands below your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keeping your core engaged and body stable, shift your weight to your left hand.
Lift your right arm off the floor, bending your elbow and pulling your hand back alongside your torso.
Return your right hand to the starting position on the floor.
Shift your weight to your right hand and repeat the movement, lifting your left arm.
about: The push up arm lift combines a standard push-up with an alternating forward arm raise, targeting the triceps and pectorals while adding a balance challenge. The single-arm lift phase engages the core and shoulders for anti-rotation stability.

name: Push-up to Toe Touch
steps: Begin in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest to the ground and perform a push-up.
As you push back up, transition into a downward-dog position by raising your hips.
Lift one hand and reach toward the opposite foot, touching or reaching toward your toe.
Return to the push-up position and repeat on the opposite side, continuing to alternate.
about: Push to toe-touch is a compound bodyweight exercise that combines a push-up with a rotational toe-touch reach. It targets the chest, triceps, and core, while the toe-touch component activates the obliques and hamstrings in a flowing sequence.

name: Quadruped Knee Lift
steps: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Brace your core and lift one knee slightly off the floor while maintaining a flat back.
Hold the position for a moment, then lower that knee and lift the other.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
Avoid allowing your hips to rotate or shift during the movement.
about: Quadruped knee lifts are a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes and core stabilizers. Hovering the knees off the floor while on all fours builds core endurance and hip stability, and is commonly used in rehabilitation and activation routines.

name: Reach to W
steps: Kneel on the floor with your torso upright and bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, reaching forward and allowing your upper back to slightly round.
Pull your hands back to the starting position at your chest.
Open your arms out to the sides, bending your elbows to form a 'W' shape while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Bring your hands back together in front of your chest.
about: The reach to W is a bodyweight exercise targeting the rhomboids and lower traps. Alternating between an overhead reach and a W position effectively activates the mid-back muscles and promotes healthy scapular movement and posture.

name: Russian Twist
steps: Sit leaning back with feet raised.
Rotate your torso side to side. Hold a weight to progress.
about: The russian twist is a classic bodyweight ab exercise that targets the obliques and core through rotational trunk movement. Performed seated with feet elevated, it challenges balance and rotational strength simultaneously.

name: Scissor Kick
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands placed beneath your lower back for support.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor and engage your core.
Raise your right leg upward while lowering your left leg, then switch in a scissoring motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor and your legs as straight as possible.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The scissor kick is a bodyweight core exercise that targets the abs and hip flexors through continuous alternating leg movement. It builds lower abdominal endurance and hip flexor strength while challenging core stability.

name: Seated Banded Row
steps: Anchor a resistance band to a fixed point at chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Step back to create tension in the band and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Pull the band toward your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the peak contraction, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The banded row is a resistance band pulling exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi and mid-back. The band provides accommodating resistance and is an accessible alternative to cable or barbell rows for developing back thickness and scapular control.

name: Seated Forward Fold
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Sit up tall with your spine lengthened and your hands resting beside your thighs.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and gently hinge forward from your hips, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Go only as far as comfortable without rounding your lower back excessively.
Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply, then slowly sit back up.
about: The gentle fold seated forward fold is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the hamstrings, with secondary engagement of the lower back and glutes. It involves hinging forward from a seated position with straight legs to gradually lengthen the posterior chain and improve flexibility.

name: Seated Knee Tuck
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands gripping the sides for support and legs extended in front of you.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor.
Bring your knees toward your chest by contracting your abs.
Pause at the top, then extend your legs back out without letting your feet touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
