about: Seated knee tucks are a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles from a bench-seated position. Drawing the knees to the chest while keeping the feet elevated challenges the lower abs and hip flexors.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot flat on the floor outside your left thigh.
Place your right hand behind you on the floor for support and wrap your left arm around your right knee.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and twist your torso to the right as far as comfortably possible.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then return to center and repeat on the opposite side.
about: Ardha matsyendrasana, or the seated spinal twist, is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the abdominal muscles and spine. It involves rotating the torso from a seated position to improve spinal mobility and engage the core and obliques.

name: Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand or kneel with your spine tall and core engaged.
Raise one arm forward to shoulder height with the elbow straight.
Slowly rotate the arm in the largest circle possible, moving it upward, backward, down, and forward.
Perform the full controlled articular rotation at a slow, deliberate pace, exploring the end range in every direction.
Complete the desired number of rotations and switch arms.
about: Shoulder car is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the deltoids, with secondary engagement of the traps and upper arms. CAR stands for controlled articular rotation; the movement involves taking the shoulder joint through its full range of motion in a slow, deliberate circle to improve joint health and mobility.

name: Shoulder Circles
steps: Stand or sit upright with your arms hanging relaxed at your sides.
Slowly roll both shoulders forward in a circular motion, moving them up toward your ears, then back, then down.
Complete the desired number of circles in the forward direction.
Reverse the motion and perform the same number of circles in the backward direction.
Keep the movement slow and controlled, feeling the muscles around the shoulder loosen with each rotation.
about: Shoulder circle is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the deltoids, with secondary engagement of the traps and upper arms. It involves rolling the shoulders in full circles to release tension, improve joint mobility, and warm up the shoulder girdle before training.

name: Side Knee Plank
steps: Lie on your side and prop yourself up on your forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your knees on top of each other with your legs bent at 90 degrees.
Lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Brace your core and avoid letting your hips drop.
Hold for the desired duration, then switch sides.
about: The side knee plank is a modified bodyweight side plank that targets the obliques with reduced difficulty. Keeping the knees bent shortens the lever arm, making it accessible as a progression toward the full side plank.

name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and prop yourself up on your forearm, with your elbow directly beneath your shoulder.
Lift your hips off the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your core engaged, your top hip pushed upward, and avoid letting your hips sag or rotate.
Hold the position for the desired duration while breathing steadily.
Lower your hips, rest, and repeat on the other side.
about: The side plank hold on elbow is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the obliques, with secondary engagement of the abs, shoulders, and glutes. It involves maintaining a rigid lateral body position on one forearm to build lateral core stability and resist spinal rotation.

name: Side Plank Arm Lift
steps: Lie on your side with your legs straight and feet stacked one on top of the other.
Prop yourself up on your forearm, ensuring your elbow is directly beneath your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor so your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Extend your top arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Hold this static position for the desired amount of time, keeping your hips elevated and core tight.
about: The side plank one arm lift is an advanced core exercise targeting the obliques through a rotational movement from a lateral plank position. Threading the arm under the body increases oblique and shoulder engagement while maintaining lateral stability.

name: Side Plank Reach Through
steps: Begin in a side plank position with your elbow on the floor and body in a straight line.
Extend your top arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Rotate your torso and reach your top arm underneath your body, threading it through.
Return to the starting position with your arm extended upward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
about: The side plank reach through is a bodyweight exercise targeting the obliques with a dynamic rotation added to the standard side plank. The reach-through motion increases thoracic rotation demand and deepens lateral core engagement.

name: Side Toe Tap
steps: Stand tall with hands on your hips.
Tap one foot out to the side and bring it back.
Alternate sides at a steady pace.
Keep your core engaged and posture upright.

name: Side to Side Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out.
Curl your upper body up and to the right, bringing your right elbow toward your right knee.
Lower back to the starting position and repeat to the left side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The side to side crunch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the obliques through lateral flexion. Alternating the crunch direction to each side creates a comprehensive oblique workout that improves lateral core strength.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Extend one leg straight, keeping your thighs parallel.
Engage your core and press through the heel of the grounded foot to lift your hips.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to the raised knee.
Pause at the top, squeezing your glute, then slowly lower your hips back down.
about: The single leg glute bridge is a unilateral bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings through single-leg hip extension. It helps identify and correct strength imbalances between sides while improving hip stability and posterior chain strength.

name: Single-Leg Toe Touch Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with your legs raised vertically toward the ceiling.
Extend your arms straight up toward your feet.
Curl your upper body off the ground and reach your hands toward your feet.
Pause at the top, squeezing your abs.
Slowly lower back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The foot touch is a bodyweight abdominal exercise performed lying on the back with legs raised. By reaching the hands toward the elevated feet, it creates a full contraction of the rectus abdominis, effectively targeting the upper and lower abs.

name: Sit-up
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outward.
Engage your abs and curl your torso all the way up until your elbows approach your knees.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Sit ups version 1 is a bodyweight core exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors and obliques. It involves a full-range sit-up movement to strengthen the anterior core and develop abdominal endurance.

name: Skater Hops
steps: Stand on your right leg with a slight knee bend.
Push off your right foot and hop laterally to land on your left foot.
Land softly on your left foot with a bent knee to absorb the impact.
Immediately push off to the right and land on your right foot.
Continue hopping side to side in a skating motion.
about: Skater hops are a plyometric bodyweight exercise targeting the quads and glutes through explosive lateral jumping. The single-leg landing improves balance, coordination, and lateral movement mechanics while building lower body power.

name: Skater Jump
steps: Stand on your right foot with your left foot lifted slightly off the ground.
Bend your right knee and push off explosively to jump laterally to the left.
Land softly on your left foot, swinging your right leg behind you and reaching your right hand toward your left foot.
Immediately push off your left foot and jump back to the right.
Continue alternating sides in a continuous skating motion for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The skater jump is a bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the glutes through a lateral bounding movement. The side-to-side explosive motion develops lateral power, single-leg stability, and cardiovascular endurance.

name: Spiderman Lunge
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders.
Step your right foot forward to land just outside your right hand.
Hold the position for a moment, feeling the stretch in your hip flexors and groin.
Return your foot to the starting plank position.
Repeat on the left side, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Spiderman lunges are a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the hip flexors. Stepping forward from a plank position into a deep lunge opens the hips and groin, and is commonly used in warm-up and mobility routines.

name: Spinal Wave
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and begin with a slow forward fold, rounding sequentially from the neck down through the spine.
Once fully folded, shift your weight into your heels and roll your spine down into a squat position.
Hold the squat briefly, engaging your core and keeping your chest open.
Drive through your heels to rise out of the squat, then sequentially uncurl your spine back to a tall standing position, head rising last.
Repeat the wave-like spinal articulation and squat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Spinal wave into squats is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the abs and spine, with secondary engagement of the lower back, quads, and glutes. It combines sequential spinal articulation with a squat to improve spinal mobility, core awareness, and lower body strength in a fluid flowing movement.

name: Split Squat Jump
steps: Stand in a lunge position with one foot forward and one foot back.
Lower into the lunge by bending both knees to 90 degrees.
Explosively jump straight up from the lunge position.
Land softly back in the same lunge stance and immediately lower into the next repetition.
Complete the desired repetitions and switch legs.
about: The split squat jump is a bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the quadriceps in a stationary lunge stance. Exploding vertically from the lunge develops single-leg power and challenges lower body endurance.

name: Sprint in Place
steps: Begin standing or jogging to warm up, then transition into a full sprint.
Drive your knees forward and pump your arms powerfully to maximize your running speed.
Maintain maximum effort for the prescribed sprint duration, typically 10-30 seconds.
Slow to a jog or walk for the designated recovery period.
Repeat the sprint and recovery intervals for the desired number of rounds.
about: Sprint interval fast running is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the hamstrings, glutes, and lower legs. It involves alternating between maximum-effort sprints and recovery periods to build cardiovascular capacity, speed, and anaerobic endurance.

name: Squat to Good Morning
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands clasped behind your head.
Perform a bodyweight squat by bending your knees and lowering your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Rise back to standing, then immediately hinge forward at the hips into a good morning, lowering your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor.
Return to standing and repeat the squat to begin the next cycle.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The warm up squat and good morning is a bodyweight combination exercise targeting the quadriceps and hamstrings. Alternating between a squat and a hip hinge pattern activates the entire lower body and prepares the posterior chain for training.

name: Standing Angel Mobility
steps: Stand tall with hands behind your head, elbows wide.
Sweep the arms out and down to your sides like a snow angel.
Bring them back up behind your head.
Move slowly and keep shoulders relaxed.

name: Standing Calf Raise
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall for balance.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly.

name: Standing Forward Fold
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge forward at the hips, pushing your hips backward while keeping your back flat and chest lifted.
Lower your torso until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, then allow your torso to round gently into a full forward fold.
Hold the folded position for 2-3 seconds, then re-engage your core and hinge back up to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Fold with hinge is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the hamstrings, with secondary engagement of the glutes and lower back. It combines a controlled hip hinge with a forward fold to dynamically stretch the posterior chain and improve hip mobility.

name: Standing Front Kick
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and shift your weight onto one leg.
Kick your free leg forward to hip height, keeping the knee extended and core engaged.
Swing the leg back behind you, extending it at the hip, and squeeze your glute at the top.
Continue swinging the leg forward and backward in a controlled, continuous motion.
Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
about: Standing front to back kick is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors, hamstrings, and abs. It involves swinging one leg forward and backward through a full sagittal arc to dynamically activate the posterior chain and improve hip mobility.

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider.
Keeping your legs straight, slowly hinge forward at your hips.
Let your arms and head hang heavy toward the floor as you lower your torso.
Lower yourself until you feel a stretch in both hamstrings.
Slowly lift your torso back up to the starting upright position.
about: The standing hamstring stretch is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the hamstrings, with secondary engagement of the glutes and lower back. It involves hinging forward over a straight leg to lengthen the hamstrings and improve flexibility in the posterior thigh.

name: Standing Hip Circles
steps: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and place your hands on your hips.
Shift your weight to one leg and lift the opposite leg in front of you.
Sweep the lifted leg out to the side in a wide, controlled circular motion to open your hip.
Bring the leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat the same motion with the other leg.
about: Hip circle version 2 is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the abs and core, with secondary engagement of the obliques, lower back, and glutes. It involves rotating the hips in full circles while standing to improve hip joint mobility, loosen the lower back, and activate the core musculature.

name: Standing Hip Stretch
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and place both hands on your hips.
Keeping your legs straight and feet flat on the floor, slowly push your hips out to one side.
Keep your upper body still and upright as you feel a gentle stretch along your outer hip.
Pause briefly, then bring your hips back to the centered starting position.
Push your hips to the opposite side.
about: Hip stretch is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the glutes and outer hip, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors and lower back. It involves a figure-4 supine position to stretch the piriformis and external hip rotators, commonly used to relieve hip tightness and lower back tension.

name: Standing Knee Raise
steps: Stand tall with hands on your hips.
Lift one knee up toward hip height.
Lower it with control and switch legs.
Keep your torso upright throughout.

name: Standing Leg Circles
steps: Stand on one leg and hold a wall or support for balance.
Lift the opposite leg slightly off the floor and begin tracing large, controlled circles with that leg.
Move the leg forward, out to the side, behind you, and back to the start in a full circular motion.
Complete the desired number of circles in one direction, then reverse.
Switch legs and repeat on the other side.
about: Leg swing in circle is a bodyweight dynamic stretching exercise targeting the glutes and hip joint, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors and hamstrings. It involves tracing full circular paths with the leg to lubricate the hip joint and improve multi-directional mobility.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
steps: Stand on one leg and bring the other foot up behind you toward your glutes.
Grasp your ankle with the corresponding hand and keep your knees close together.
Stand tall, keeping your hips level and your core engaged.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling tension along the front of your thigh.
Release and repeat on the other leg.
about: The standing quadriceps stretch is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the hip flexors and lower legs. It involves pulling the heel toward the glutes while standing to lengthen the front of the thigh and improve quad flexibility.

name: Standing Side Bend
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise one arm overhead and gently bend your torso to the opposite side, letting your other arm reach toward the floor.
Smoothly return to the upright position, extending both arms wide to the sides to open your chest.
Raise your opposite arm overhead and bend your torso to the other side.
Return to the center with your arms extended wide.
about: Upper body cool down stretch is a bodyweight stretching exercise targeting the deltoids, with secondary engagement of the traps, chest, and upper arms. It alternates between a chest-rounded forward stretch and an open-chest backward stretch to systematically release tension across the upper body after training.

name: Starfish Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms and legs extended outward in an X shape.
Simultaneously lift your right arm and left leg, crunching your torso to bring them toward each other.
Touch or reach toward your foot at the top of the movement.
Lower back to the starting X position.
Repeat on the opposite side, lifting your left arm and right leg.
about: The starfish crunch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles through a diagonal cross-body crunch from an X-shaped lying position. The movement develops full abdominal and oblique engagement with a wide range of motion.

name: Sumo Squat
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulders, toes turned out.
Sit hips down between your heels, keeping chest up.
Push knees out over toes at the bottom.
Drive through heels to stand tall.

name: Sumo Squat Tap
steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes turned outward.
Lower into a sumo squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
From the squat, reach one hand across to tap the opposite foot or the floor beside it.
Return to the squat and repeat on the other side in an alternating tapping motion.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The sumo tap is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hip adductors in a wide-stance squat position. Alternating reaches add a lateral core challenge and improve hip mobility and dynamic balance.

name: Superman
steps: Lie face-down with arms overhead.
Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor, hold briefly, lower.
about: The superman hold is a bodyweight posterior chain exercise targeting the lower back erectors through a prone hyperextension hold. Lifting both arms and legs simultaneously engages the entire back and glutes, building spinal extension endurance.

name: T-Spine Rotation
steps: Start in a quadruped position with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Place one hand behind your head with your elbow pointing outward.
Rotate your upper body, opening your elbow toward the ceiling as far as comfortable.
Hold briefly at the end range, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
about: T-spine rotation is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the thoracic spine and lower back. The controlled rotation improves thoracic mobility, reduces stiffness, and is commonly used in warm-up routines and injury prevention protocols.

name: TVA Activation (Drawing In)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, or stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Take a relaxed breath in, allowing your abdomen to expand naturally.
As you exhale, slowly draw your navel inward toward your spine without holding your breath.
Hold the contraction gently for 5-10 seconds while breathing normally.
Release and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: TVA activation, also known as the drawing in maneuver, is a bodyweight rehabilitation exercise targeting the transverse abdominis. The gentle inward draw of the navel activates the deepest core stabilizing muscle and is a foundational movement in core rehabilitation and posture correction programs.

name: Thoracic Bridge
steps: Begin in a tabletop position on your hands and knees.
Place one hand behind your head with your elbow pointing outward.
Rotate your torso to bring that elbow toward the floor between your arm and knee.
Then rotate in the opposite direction, opening your chest and reaching that elbow toward the ceiling.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and switch sides.
about: The reach back thoracic bridge is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the lats, with secondary engagement of the chest, lower back, and shoulders. It involves rotating through the thoracic spine from a quadruped position to improve upper back mobility and shoulder health.

name: Toe Tap
steps: Lie on your back with your legs raised vertically, forming a 90-degree angle at the hips.
Extend your arms straight up toward your feet.
Curl your upper body off the ground and reach your fingertips toward your toes.
Lightly tap your toes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The toe tap is a bodyweight abdominal exercise performed lying on the back with legs raised vertically. Reaching upward to tap the toes creates a strong contraction of the rectus abdominis and engages the hip flexors throughout.

name: Toe Touch Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back and raise your legs straight up perpendicular to the floor.
Extend your arms toward the ceiling.
Engage your core and reach your hands toward your feet by lifting your shoulders off the ground.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the floor.
about: The toe touch crunch is a bodyweight ab exercise performed with legs vertical. Reaching toward the feet from this elevated position increases the range of motion and demands greater abdominal contraction than a standard crunch.

name: Tuck Jump
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and bend slightly at the knees.
Explosively jump upward as high as possible.
At the peak of the jump, tuck your knees toward your chest.
Release your knees and land softly with a slight bend in the knees.
Immediately perform the next repetition.
about: The tuck jump is a plyometric exercise targeting the quads and developing explosive lower body power. The knee tuck at the peak of the jump challenges hip flexor strength and cardiovascular conditioning simultaneously.

name: Twisting Sit-up
steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with elbows pointing outward.
Engage your core and curl your torso upward, simultaneously rotating your right elbow toward your left knee.
Lower back to the starting position, then curl up again and rotate your left elbow toward your right knee.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Twisted sit-ups are a bodyweight core exercise targeting the obliques, with secondary engagement of the abs and hip flexors. They combine the sit-up movement with a rotational twist to effectively train the lateral core musculature and improve rotational strength.

name: V-Up
steps: Lie flat with arms overhead.
Lift your legs and torso to touch your toes, then lower.
about: The v-up, also known as a jackknife, is an advanced bodyweight core exercise that simultaneously engages the upper and lower abs. By lifting both the torso and legs together, it creates a full abdominal contraction and challenges hip flexor strength.

name: Wall Sit
steps: Slide down a wall until your knees are at 90°.
Hold. Log seconds as reps.
about: The wall sit is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the quadriceps. Holding the seated wall position develops quad endurance, lower body stability, and muscular strength without any dynamic movement.

name: Warrior I Lunge Stretch
steps: Step one foot forward into a wide lunge, keeping your front knee bent at approximately 90 degrees directly over your ankle.
Turn your back foot out at a 45-degree angle and press through the outer edge of that foot.
Square your hips toward the front of the mat as much as possible.
Raise both arms overhead with palms facing each other and draw your shoulders down away from your ears.
Hold for 20-30 seconds while breathing steadily, then switch sides.
about: Warrior 1 alignment is a bodyweight yoga exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes, hamstrings, and shoulders. It involves holding a deep lunge position with arms raised overhead to simultaneously strengthen the lower body, open the hip flexors, and develop postural awareness.

name: Wide Push-up
steps: Place your hands well outside shoulder width.
Lower your chest to the floor and push back up.
about: The wide grip push up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest with increased emphasis on the outer pectoral muscles. The wider hand position reduces triceps involvement and places greater stress on the chest, making it an effective variation for developing chest width and strength.

name: Windshield Wiper
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended out to the sides for stability.
Bend your knees and bring them together above your hips at a 90-degree angle.
Rotate your knees slowly to one side, lowering them toward the floor.
Bring your knees back to center and rotate to the other side.
Continue alternating sides in a windshield wiper motion for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The warm up wiper is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the obliques and spinal rotators. The side-to-side leg rotation from the lying position loosens the lower back and activates the core before training.

name: Wrist Circle
steps: Extend your arms in front of you at shoulder height.
Make fists with both hands and begin rotating your wrists in slow, full circles.
Perform the desired number of circles in one direction, then reverse.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
about: Wrist circles are a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the forearms and wrist joint. The circular motion improves wrist flexibility, reduces stiffness, and is used as a warm-up before exercises involving grip and pressing.
